<thought>To determine the number of carbonyl (C=O) groups, the most direct approach is to examine the ^13C NMR spectrum and count the signals that appear in the typical carbonyl chemical shift region (≈190–220 ppm). This avoids ambiguity that can arise from overlapping IR peaks. I will request the carbon NMR spectrum for the sample and then count the carbonyl signals.</thought>
